symptom: Inside `while true`, an if/else whose arms join before one more step (`set $i = $i + 1`) and the jump back was described with that step as the last statement of the THEN arm. The stored flow was right; rebuilding from the text (drop + create, as MDL-V1-REBUILD asks) made the ELSE arm skip it, so a counter loop never ended.
cause: Three reachability walks in the split/join pairing ignored that the loop header is on a cycle: findMergeForSplit's bypass filter saw the join's 'downstream' run round the loop back into the split's own arms and rejected the real join; resolveNestedMergeID saw the header 'reach' the inner join and swapped the header in as the split's join. Fixing those two alone broke the opposite shape (exit in the ELSE arm, SUB_UserTaskView_Migrate): the THEN arm, going round, reached the ELSE arm through the split and was paired with it — so the branch-distance walk needs the same barrier.
insight: Same rule as the 2026-10-21 microflowgraph finding, in a different walker: every reachability question asked on behalf of one split must stop at that split, because a walk that passes back through it has gone round a loop. Apply it to ALL the walks for the split at once — fixing only the walk the repro exercises regressed another loop shape, which only a describe diff over the whole TestApp corpus (before vs after binary) showed; the unit suite stayed green.
